subject: BlueHarbor: subprocessor roster + DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Emily Parker <emily.parker@blueharbor.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>; procurement@blueharbor.com
Cc: security@blueharbor.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster & DPA addendum

Marcus — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Security asked me to follow up with two things we need to complete our vendor onboarding checklist:

1) A current subprocessor roster (names, scope, country of processing) for any third parties involved in telemetry, logging, storage, KMS/HSM, and CDN.
2) A proposed DPA addendum that covers our residency and escrow responsibilities; we may provide a redline but it helps to start from your suggested text.

Can you send both by EOD Friday? If you have an issues list or need an NDA for any attachments, flag it.

Thanks,
Emily Parker
Vendor Onboarding | BlueHarbor Inc.
attachments: none
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster & DPA addendum

Emily — appreciate the clear ask. Quick plan and what's attached: 

- Attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx (roster + country + processing purpose), kms_hsm_statement.pdf (short summary of KMS/HSM controls), and a DPA addendum template we often use for residency carve-outs.
- Timing: roster + KMS doc available now (attached). Ben will send a DPA addendum redline tomorrow; Naomi will confirm which processors have EU/US-only routing options.
- Outstanding: a few telemetry partners are flagged as temporary proxies during edge rollout; we'll mark those as "transient" in the roster and note retention windows.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call Thursday to walk the procurement and security teams through the roster and our minimal-privilege controls.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx; kms_hsm_statement.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@blueharbor.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster & DPA addendum

Emily / Marcus — a couple of clarifications from Security side: 

- The KMS/HSM note is intentionally high-level in the attached PDF; if BlueHarbor requires vendor-managed HSM attestations we can provide a scoped statement for the specific processors (we use AWS KMS w/ custom key policies for hosted accounts and an HSM-backed KMS option for Dedicated/private installations).
- For telemetry/observability processors: we have two categories — (A) telemetry collectors that only receive anonymized prefixes (no customer PII) and (B) observability export sinks that can contain trace identifiers. Category A processors are allowed global routing. Category B processors we can configure to route to US-only or EU-only endpoints on request.

Please confirm which of the following you need from us: full SOC2 evidence for any listed processor, HSM attestation for KMS-backed keys, or export-scoped dataflow diagrams. I can pull the scoped artifacts next week.

-Naomi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: Emily Parker <emily.parker@blueharbor.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster & DPA addendum

Naomi — thanks, that helps. For our onboarding lane we need: 

- SOC2 evidence for any processor that handles observability export sinks (Category B).
- HSM attestation for the KMS option if you propose using the HSM-backed keys for our Dedicated environment; otherwise, KMS key policy detail is sufficient.
- A short export-scoped dataflow PNG for each Category B processor showing where logs and traces are retained and for how long.

Also — procurement will send a DPA redline tomorrow. Can you confirm whether the DPA addendum you mentioned supports a 30-day SL release for temporary processors engaged during migration? If not, we'll include language in our redline.

Thanks,
Emily
attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Parker <emily.parker@blueharbor.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster & DPA addendum

Emily — attaching the DPA addendum redline (dpa-addendum-BH-redline.docx). A few notes inline: 

- We can accept a 30-day temporary processor SL for clearly scoped migration windows; we'll include an automated notification requirement when a transient processor is added and a retention/escrow trigger in the addendum.
- For HSM attestation: if BlueHarbor requires an external third-party attestation we can provide our HSM vendor's statement; internal KMS key policy extracts are included in the kms_hsm_statement.pdf attached earlier.
- We'll produce the SOC2 evidence packet for Category B processors and short dataflow PNGs by next Wednesday.

Let us know if you prefer a live walkthrough with Security + Procurement on Thursday morning — happy to set that up.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: dpa-addendum-BH-redline.docx
